(4) positive recognition = SIX required conjuncts, 11-step sequence (section 33): resolve canonical <HPAC_PROTECTED_ROOT> (no input); resolve canonical configured agent principal; validate root ownership + configured-agent exclusion + safe ancestors (_validate_production_boundary re-scoped per F-1); verify {device,inode} root-identity binding; load descriptor no-follow + validate closed schema + digest + protected_root_identity + ownership/mode + provenance_ref + state==ACTIVE; load current-generation record + require descriptor.generation == current_generation + digest match; verify current context is NOT the configured agent principal; perform O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW positive write probe under .authority/; verify calling module is an authorized factory consumer; mint the process-local operation-scoped PRODUCTION HPACWriterCapability; record issuance audit evidence. (5) descriptor identity HPAC-PAWA-AUTHORITY-DESCRIPTOR/1.0 at <HPAC_PROTECTED_ROOT>/.authority/deployment-owner.json -- single canonical descriptor, HPAC-REQ-089 canonicalised, create-only per generation, read-back verified. (6) CLOSED descriptor schema (section 14): artifact_schema_version (const), descriptor_digest (self-excluding SHA-256), anchor_id (hpaw-<hex32>), installation_id (hpawi-<hex32>), protected_root_identity ({device,inode}), authority_namespace (const '.authority'), deployment_owner_role (closed vocabulary {HPAC_PROTECTED_ADMIN}, grammar ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$, one member, no wildcard/all/root), configured_agent_exclusion_binding (closed object {excluded_principal_kind: const PCAE_CONFIGURED_AGENT_PRINCIPAL, exclusion_basis: const OS_FILESYSTEM_WRITE_AUTHORITY} -- records KIND and BASIS, not a mutable uid a caller could reinterpret), generation (int >= 1), created_at (RFC3339 UTC trusted clock), supersedes (null for gen 1 else {previous_generation, previous_descriptor_digest}), provenance_ref (HPAC-WRITER-PROVENANCE/1.0 record key), state (closed {ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, REVOKED}); NO mutable human-readable authority fact a caller could reinterpret. (7) descriptor != human identity (section 15) -- establishes an installation/deployment administrative authority anchor (a filesystem-ownership role + its currentness); does NOT prove civil identity / current human presence / runtime approval intent; the human principal being enrolled still performs the full RHAMP-001 FIDO2 ceremony. (8) root/installation identity binding (section 16) -- the descriptor is trusted ONLY when it resolves at the canonical path under the canonical protected root whose {device, inode} matches both the live stat and the HPAC-STORE-AUTHORITY/1.0 manifest and whose provenance record's root_identity_digest matches; 'machine identity' as a vague concept SHALL NOT be used; a copied descriptor or whole root does not automatically validate. (9) descriptor ownership/mode (section 17) -- normative property first (macOS/Linux adapters second): owned by the deployment owner, not group/other-writable, no agent write by mode/group/ACL; if permissions become weaker than the contract permits at any validation point -> fail closed (descriptor_wrong_mode / descriptor_wrong_owner), never 'repair', never proceed. (10) NO path-only trust (section 18) -- correct path + valid closed structure != trusted descriptor; trust additionally requires ownership/mode + root-identity binding + current generation + provisioning provenance + state==ACTIVE + (for minting) configured-agent exclusion + positive write probe + not-configured-agent context. (11) descriptor provenance (section 19) -- each descriptor write emits an HPAC-WRITER-PROVENANCE/1.0 record (the existing idiom); a new cryptographic signing key is NOT required (Candidate C rejected for v1). (12) F-3 INCORPORATED -- section 14 adds generation + a closed supersedes object; section 20 (HPAC-PAWA-REQ-047..050): generation is monotonic, installation-local, strictly increasing; initial = exactly 1; every rotation = previous + 1; unique per installation_id; the CURRENT generation is anchored by a new protected HPAC-PAWA-CURRENT-GENERATION/1.0 record (current-generation.json), create-only at provisioning, updated only by a deployment-owner atomic replace whose new value is exactly old + 1; recognition requires descriptor.generation == current_generation and a digest match; generation is NOT advisory; if monotonic atomic-replace with read-back is unavailable the implementing phase STOPS (BLOCKED). Section 21 (HPAC-PAWA-REQ-051..053): a previously superseded valid descriptor SHALL NOT become current merely because its bytes are restored -- a bytes-only rollback to generation N while current_generation is M > N -> descriptor_generation_stale; a full paired rollback requires being the deployment owner (in the model's trust boundary -- the contract does not and need not prevent the deployment owner reverting their own installation); a restored old whole root is additionally caught by the {device, inode} binding. (13) machine migration / reprovisioning (section 22) -- legitimate migration = the deployment owner performs an explicit out-of-band provision on the new host / new protected root: a new installation_id, a fresh {device,inode} root identity, generation reset to 1, a fresh current-generation record, a fresh provenance chain; anchor_id MAY be carried forward or minted fresh; rollback/replay = restoring files without a new installation_id and without a new root identity -> caught by sections 16/20/21; copying protected files alone is NEVER sufficient. (14) initial out-of-band bootstrap (section 23) -- a standalone script (recommended scripts/hpac_protected_root_admin.py provision), never a pcae CLI subcommand, never agent-invocable, run by an operator logged in as the deployment owner; creates the 0700 root, the HPAC-STORE-AUTHORITY/1.0 manifest (create-only), the descriptor at generation 1 with a fresh anchor_id and installation_id, current-generation.json at 1, correct ownership/mode, a durable provisioning provenance/audit record; completes WITHOUT any existing HPACWriterCapability (filesystem primitives) -- a filesystem provisioning act by the OS deployment owner, outside PCAE's authority model entirely; NON-CIRCULAR; does NOT require, consult, or create a FIDO2 credential, an enrolled human principal, an AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal, a RHAMP-001 ceremony, a PB decision, an RE result, or any runtime capability. (15) bootstrap repeatability (section 24) -- NOT silently repeatable over an existing valid installation; a second provision -> fail closed (duplicate_bootstrap) or explicitly enter the distinct rotation/reprovisioning procedure; never a silent authority reset, never a generation reset over a live installation; an idempotent no-op is permitted only when byte-identical. (16) recognition predicates 1-6 (sections 25-32): canonical root (no caller/repo/env/cwd replacement); configured-agent exclusion (_effective_write_access against the CONFIGURED principal's ids returns False + ancestors safe -- NOT current_euid != some_agent_uid, NOT os.geteuid() != 0); descriptor trust (canonical path + closed schema + root-identity + current generation + ownership/mode + provenance + state==ACTIVE); positive write authority (operation-based, NOT os.access() alone -- an O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW create + write + fsync + close + unlink of a randomly-named sentinel under .authority/; EACCES/EPERM/EROFS/any failure -> write_probe_failed); not-configured-agent current-context (explicit negative assertion against the canonical configured-agent identity source, never a caller boolean); authorized factory consumer (only through the admin writer module's factory from an EXACT authorized consumer -- no general public API, no pcae CLI path, no agent-reachable entry). (17) write-probe target (section 29) -- a dedicated ephemeral sentinel under .authority/, never arbitrary production state, never the descriptor / current-generation / manifest / provenance; O_EXCL (no destructive overwrite), no symlink follow, verify actual create/write/fsync/close/remove; cleanup failure handled explicitly as write_probe_failed / protected_root_untrusted, never ignored. (18) TOCTOU (section 30) -- ordered sequence (validate root+identity -> validate descriptor+generation against the SAME resolved root -> probe against the SAME resolved .authority/ path -> mint immediately within the same process/context); NO promise of absolute TOCTOU elimination; the capability's authority is RE-VERIFIED at every record_write / _write (require_writer + _ensure_root + _validate_production_boundary re-run on every mutation), the registry's expected_current compare-and-write rejects a stale write -- a probe->mint->write race cannot WIDEN authority. (19) sudo/euid prohibition (section 34) -- 'if os.geteuid() == 0: allow', 'if os.getuid() == 0: allow', 'if SUDO_USER in os.environ: allow', 'if os.environ.get(SUDO_UID): allow' SHALL NOT appear as the normative positive predicate; sudo/root MAY be part of the underlying OS mechanism but neither euid==0 nor any SUDO_* env var is by itself the positive predicate; euid==0 alone mints NOTHING; euid/sudo MAY be a non-authoritative audit annotation only. (20) privileged-wrong-principal claim boundary (section 35) -- HPAC-REQ-023 is verified as an OS-authority / installation-role construct, not a specific-human cryptographic or civil identity; therefore ANY process that legitimately holds the deployment-owner OS filesystem write authority over the specific admin-owned <HPAC_PROTECTED_ROOT> and presents a valid current descriptor and is not the configured agent principal SATISFIES the anchor; the contract does NOT claim to identify WHICH human or WHICH privileged account; a different local admin/root without legitimate filesystem write to THIS deployment's protected root fails the probe and the ownership check; if a future requirement demands more (a specific enrolled administrative human identity for the WRITER path) that is a MAJOR and a new adjudication -- v1.0 SHALL NOT silently require it or claim it. (21) production writer factory (section 36) -- given a successful section 33 sequence, mints exactly one process-local operation-scoped PRODUCTION HPACWriterCapability bound to the resolved PRODUCTION HPACStoreAuthority instance's _seal via the existing _WRITER_CONSTRUCTOR_SEAL discipline; conceptual symbol HPACStoreAuthority.production_writer(operation, *, principal_id=None, credential_id=None) or a repository-derived equivalent (semantics fixed, not the exact name); does NOT weaken any existing HPACWriterCapability semantics; the PRODUCTION capability is STRICTLY narrower than the fixture writer (operation-scoped and single-use); NO new broad admin token; ProtectedAdminCapability stays legacy fixture-only. (22) module boundary (section 37) -- a separate admin-only production module (recommended src/pcae/core/hpac_protected_admin_writer.py); ordinary agent / runtime / Gate / pcae CLI code SHALL NOT import it directly or transitively; NOT a pcae CLI subcommand, not in any command dispatch table, not on any plugin import path, not a repository-integration consumer; the provisioning / enrollment / recovery tools are standalone scripts/ entrypoints; the consumer inventory is EXACT -- an enumerated list of specific module dotted-paths; NO wildcard, prefix, fnmatch, glob. (23) authorized consumers (section 38) -- the closed categories: the bounded protected principal administration tool; the first-credential bootstrap / enrollment tool; the recovery / re-bootstrap tool; NOT authorized: ordinary agent commands, any pcae CLI subcommand, Gate 5/6/7/8/9/10 or any gate coordinator, the runtime adapter, any plugin runtime, repository callbacks/hooks, the ordinary task lifecycle, the session/handoff machinery, core/agent.py, cli.py, commands/**. (24) consumer inventory guard (section 39) -- .1R.30R.3 SHALL add exact source/import consumer-inventory tests (the HBDC-REQ-056/066 pattern: a text-scan of cli.py / commands/** / core/agent.py asserting the admin writer module name and the production_writer symbol never appear as an import; and an assertion that the operations are standalone scripts/ files, not pcae CLI subcommands); any NEW production consumer fails the guard until explicitly added to the section 38 inventory AND the contract is amended; NO glob/fnmatch/prefix broadening ever. (25) HPACWriterCapability class (section 40) -- reuses the existing class unchanged in shape (__slots__ + __reduce__ raises); the PRODUCTION class meaning: authority_class is HPACAuthorityClass.PRODUCTION, minted only by the section 33 sequence, that HumanPrincipalRegistryStore._writer() and the section 42 stores will accept for exactly one bounded mutation; NOT obtainable by writer() (still raises for every non-fixture class), legacy_fixture_writer(), object.__new__, copy/deepcopy/pickle, or reconstruction from known field values. (26) issuance inputs (section 41) -- binds EXACTLY (least authority): the resolved PRODUCTION HPACStoreAuthority instance's _seal; the role (one of the section 42 writer roles); the subject (the target principal_id or credential_id, or the enrollment-transaction id where a credential id does not yet exist); the operation enum; recorded in issuance audit evidence but NOT as capability fields: anchor_id, installation_id, descriptor generation, protected_root_identity, an operation_id, the issuance trusted-clock timestamp, the issuer/factory identity. (27) operation scope (section 42) -- a PRODUCTION writer capability SHALL NOT authorize arbitrary HPAC writes; the closed set: enroll_principal, revoke_principal, enroll_credential (+ the RHAMP-FIDO2-CREDENTIAL/1.0 sidecar + RHAMP-COUNTER-STATE/1.0 for one credential), revoke_credential, initialize_credential_sidecar_state; SHALL NOT authorize writing an HPAC-PROOF/2.0, a lifecycle event, an HPAC-PRESENTATION-EVIDENCE/2.0, an HPAC-AUTHORITY-CONSUMPTION/2.1 record, or any Gate-5/Gate-9 artifact (those remain the trusted verifier's, is_verifier_authenticated_principal boundary); SHALL NOT issue a runtime approval, a PB permission, an RE result, or a DispatchEnvelope; binds the protected-root target (the fixed registry path + the fixed per-credential sidecar/counter-state paths); NOT an 'HPAC admin forever' capability. (28) principal scope (section 43) -- bound to the EXACT principal_id via subject; a capability minted for principal A SHALL NOT write principal B (require_writer subject mismatch -> reject; target_scope_invalid). (29) credential scope (section 44) -- for an existing credential, bound to the exact credential_id; for enroll_credential (fresh opaque hpc-<hex> not existing until the write), bound to the enrollment-transaction id (an operation_id reserved before the ceremony) + the target principal_id; NOT over-bound to a credential_id that does not yet exist. (30) process-local (section 45) -- not durable, never written to disk, never serialised to JSON, never exported, never transmitted over IPC/socket/network/pipe; the _authority_seal is the specific HPACStoreAuthority instance's private object() -- meaningful only within the minting process. (31) non-bearer (section 46) -- possession of an object with structurally identical fields does NOT establish authority; valid only if produced by the canonical PRODUCTION writer factory in this process and recognised by require_writer's IDENTITY check (writer._authority_seal is self._seal), not a value comparison; structure is not authority. (32) non-serializable (section 47) -- pickle/copy/deepcopy rejected (__reduce__ raises); JSON serialisation as authority rejected (no serialiser exists; a hand-built dict is not a capability); object.__new__ + known field values rejected (fails the seal-identity check + the live root re-probe); cross-process transfer rejected (a new process has a fresh _seal); an audit projection MAY serialise NON-authoritative facts only (never the _authority_seal, never reconstructable into a working capability). (33) restart invalidation (section 48) -- a process restart invalidates ALL previously minted PRODUCTION writer capabilities (a new HPACStoreAuthority instance has a fresh _seal); a new administrative operation after a restart SHALL re-run the full section 33 sequence and mint a fresh capability. (34) one-operation / short-lived (section 49) -- authorizes EXACTLY ONE administrative operation or ONE bounded enrollment transaction; SHALL NOT be reused for a second operation; .1R.30R.3 SHALL implement the single-use invariant (a one-shot wrapper, or the admin tool process exits after one operation, or the capability is consumed/marked spent on first record_write) -- after one successful mutation the same capability object SHALL NOT authorize a second record_write/_write (a second attempt -> capability_stale); if implementing single-use requires a type change beyond the current __slots__ it is ADDITIVE (a spent flag), never a weakening; the enclosing admin tool is short-lived (one operation per invocation, process exits after). (35) rotation (section 50) -- a distinct, explicit deployment-owner operation (never implicit, never a side effect of re-running provision); writes a new deployment-owner.json at generation = old + 1 with supersedes = {previous_generation, previous_descriptor_digest}; emits its provenance record; then atomically replaces current-generation.json to current_generation = old + 1 with the new descriptor digest; then marks the old descriptor state = SUPERSEDED (or removes it -- the current-generation anchor is authoritative); after rotation the old generation SHALL NOT mint new capabilities; prefer fail-closed (MAY invalidate in-flight capabilities on a detected rotation). (36) revocation (section 51) -- the closed state model {ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, REVOKED}; a REVOKED anchor -> recognition fails closed (descriptor_revoked), NO PRODUCTION writer is minted until a new provision/rotation re-establishes an ACTIVE descriptor; revocation is a deployment-owner filesystem operation. (37) recovery / reprovisioning (section 52) -- explicit procedures, each an out-of-band deployment-owner act, NEVER from repository state / user config / an environment variable / a NON_REAL fixture: protected-root damage -> provision --repair or re-provision on a fresh location; lost installation descriptor -> same; host migration -> the section 22 legitimate-migration path; deployment-owner administrative reprovisioning -> explicit rotation or re-provision; total-principal-loss recovery (HPAC-REQ-065, RHAMP-REQ-050) repeats the RHAMP-001 bootstrap ceremony which requires a PRODUCTION writer via this anchor -- the anchor is a prerequisite, NOT a fallback. (38) clone / snapshot rule (section 53) -- a copied snapshot of an old protected root does NOT automatically regain authority if the current installation/generation state says otherwise; the stable verifiable identity is the protected-root {device, inode} bound in HPAC-STORE-AUTHORITY/1.0 and echoed in the descriptor's protected_root_identity and installation_id; only a byte-identical restore to the original device/inode may still validate. (39) audit evidence (section 54) -- durable audit facts SHALL be recorded for bootstrap/provisioning, descriptor rotation, revocation, capability issuance, administrative operation result; AUDIT EVIDENCE IS NOT CAPABILITY -- a provenance / issuance-evidence / enrollment-evidence record proves a write happened, it does NOT mint / restore / stand in for an HPACWriterCapability, and SHALL NOT become bearer authority. (40) capability issuance audit (section 55) -- each successful section 33 issuance records a durable HPAC-PAWA-ISSUANCE-EVIDENCE/1.0 event with exactly: event_schema_version (const), operation_id, operation, anchor_id, installation_id, descriptor_generation, protected_root_identity, target_principal_id (or null), target_credential_id (or null), enrollment_transaction_id (or null), issued_at (trusted clock), issuer, result/status (issued), capability_identifier (a non-authoritative opaque id/digest, NOT the seal), optionally context_annotation (the non-authoritative euid/sudo note); SHALL NOT serialise the _authority_seal, any capability secret, or anything from which a working capability could be reconstructed; a FAILED attempt records the terminal section 56 code + the same identifying context. (41) failure taxonomy (section 56) -- the closed 21-value pawa_failure_code vocabulary: protected_root_missing, protected_root_untrusted, agent_principal_unknown, agent_has_protected_write_authority, descriptor_missing, descriptor_malformed, descriptor_wrong_owner, descriptor_wrong_mode, descriptor_root_identity_mismatch, descriptor_installation_mismatch, descriptor_generation_stale, descriptor_revoked, write_probe_failed, current_context_is_agent, unauthorized_factory_consumer, operation_scope_invalid, target_scope_invalid, capability_stale, duplicate_bootstrap, reconstruction_attempt, internal_fail_closed; every terminal failure of provisioning / recognition / issuance maps DETERMINISTICALLY to exactly one; free-form authority-decision reason strings prohibited; .1R.30R.3 finalises the exact identifiers after source review; the set is closed and complete for v1.0 (adding a code for a genuinely new terminal path is a MINOR). (42) RHAMP terminal-reason mapping (section 57) -- RHAMP-001 v1.0 section 49's terminal_reason_code vocabulary is frozen at 41 values and RHAMP-001 SHALL NOT be edited by this phase; where a PAWA failure occurs DURING a RHAMP-001 first-credential enrollment/bootstrap ceremony and a RHAMP lifecycle event can be persisted, the PAWA failure maps to exactly one existing RHAMP terminal_reason_code: descriptor_* + agent_principal_unknown + duplicate_bootstrap -> #1 bootstrap_authority_unproven; current_context_is_agent + agent_has_protected_write_authority + unauthorized_factory_consumer + write_probe_failed -> #2 enrollment_not_protected_admin; protected_root_missing + protected_root_untrusted -> #40 protected_root_invalid; operation_scope_invalid + target_scope_invalid + capability_stale + reconstruction_attempt + internal_fail_closed -> #41 internal_verification_error; NO new terminal_reason_code is required or authorised; if a future PAWA failure genuinely has no semantically valid RHAMP mapping that is a BLOCKED-on-contract-compatibility condition for the phase that discovers it -- it does NOT silently edit RHAMP-001; outside a RHAMP ceremony the pawa_failure_code is the terminal record. (43) PAWA failure != runtime denial (section 58) -- PAWA failures are ADMINISTRATIVE WRITER failures; they SHALL NOT become PB decisions or reason ids, RE reason ids or no-go ids, runtime-capability reasons, Gate7Result fields, or a DispatchEnvelope rejection; the PAWA and RHAMP/PB/RE vocabularies stay separate. (44) root TCB claim boundary (section 60) -- a fully privileged OS administrator within the trusted protected-root boundary can alter protected administrative state by design (that party IS or can act as the deployment owner); HPAC-PAWA-001 protects against the CONFIGURED agent principal, the same normal-user domain on a two-principal deployment, and repository/caller/environment/cwd/task/Git/session influence; it does NOT attempt to defend against a hostile root TCB (HBDC-001 section 18 limit, inherited). (45) two-principal requirement (section 61) -- the configured agent principal SHALL be OS-separable from the deployment-owner protected-admin authority (a distinct OS account whose write authority to <HPAC_PROTECTED_ROOT> the configured agent principal provably lacks); if they share identical effective protected-root write authority (a single-account host, or a misconfigured two-account host where the agent has ACL/group write) -> REAL PRODUCTION writer issuance is INELIGIBLE, recognition fails closed (agent_has_protected_write_authority / protected_root_untrusted), NO PRODUCTION writer is minted; fail closed, NEVER a downgrade to a weaker check. (46) local / offline (section 62) -- NO network service, NO cloud token, NO external identity provider, NO online key verification, NO remote attestation; all operations are local filesystem. (47) macOS / Linux abstraction (section 63) -- freezes normative security properties, not implementation-specific commands (a deployment owner exists and owns <HPAC_PROTECTED_ROOT>; the configured agent principal provably lacks write; ownership/mode/ACL is verifiable; a positive O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW write probe is available; no repo/caller/env/cwd influence); implementation adapters MAY differ per OS under .1R.30R.3; _effective_write_access / _ancestor_chain_safe already span both. (48) no keychain / pinned-key requirement (section 64) -- because Candidates C (admin-signed record + pinned key) and D (OS keychain/keyring) were rejected for v1.0, HPAC-PAWA-001 v1.0 does NOT require an administrator signing key, a pinned public verification key, an OS keychain/keyring secret, or a password/passphrase store; the implementation SHALL NOT reintroduce any as an authority input; a future MAJOR MAY add a signing model if a remote/multi-host topology is authorised.
